module_mood_contract: diagnostic directness. Plain placements, thin spots marked, no reassurance.

rules_evaluated.evidence: L3-L5: names the lenses AFTER the notes exercise ("The notes you just wrote are half of a diagnosis"); it teaches vocabulary (ADKAR, adoption curve, Kotter) mid-module immediately before the install prompt that uses them, which is the mid-module vocabulary slot; it names no pattern the student has yet to live. Harm (abstract claim told before the experience) absent: the experience is the notes just written.

rules_evaluated.na_reason: module mood is diagnostic directness, not a contrast-mood learn-by-doing-then-name module

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nE 'M[0-9]|[Mm]odule' on body L1-39 -> 0 hits (run). Closest: L3 "The notes you just wrote" and L38 "what you are about to put on the page" bind to the neighbouring exercises, but name no module number, module or file, and the placement is the maintainer-recorded design; harm (lecture not re-placeable, forward-reference rot) is mild and no module name to move.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers L5 "We bring the lenses", L15 "You bring your people", L21 "Agents multiply both", L27 "Where the team sits on the curve". Closest to failing squint: L15 ("You bring your people") is half of a paired frame, but the body at L17 hands over the concrete (who trusts whom, quiet teacher); L21 truthful, body L25 "It multiplies what you bring. It replaces neither half." No em-dashes (grep -c '—' on body -> 0), no bare arc labels, no duplicate headers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded, not just its header (§4's sibling).
A prompt inside a lecture is a trainer show-and-tell, never a room follow-along.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Module contract (see-your-team maintainer block): diagnostic directness, plain placements, no reassurance. L25 "Where your notes are thin, the agent's work is thin, however good the framework" is the closest to soft-pedalling and instead holds the direct register. Student leaves wanting the placements made; sets up the install exercise without doing it. Trace mood 8 at the one teaching beat and 8 at close; all four slides are teaching beats, none setup.

L23 "Your people without theory leaves you where you are now, with good instincts and no way to test them" is not-knowing (no way to test) and credits the instincts; L17 "the most sceptical about agents, and why both are true" is curiosity, not blame. Nothing says the student did wrong.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Title and headers lead with the discipline (L1 "Theory times people-knowledge", L5 lenses, L21 multiplication). Closest: L23 "generic advice: address resistance, find champions" is the negative case the discipline addresses, sitting inside the body not a header.

Facets checked: front-run: names ADKAR/curve/Kotter that the same-module install prompt uses (see-your-team maintainer: Team Knowledge places on ADKAR + curve), no M2 asking or M3 export content; nothing here pre-empts the Decision Journal or the backfire lecture. Big Idea ("knowledge of your people is the input nobody else has") honoured at L15-L19, L25. Arc: L3 receives the notes exercise, L38 hands to putting the spread on the page = install exercise. Mood does not resolve early: L13 "They cannot tell you what this team will do" leaves the diagnosis open.
